clue.text: Last months keeping 99 in picture with a range of backgrounds

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so these months hold a piece between them

parts.note: a mural is a picture painted on a wall

indicators.note: in places the whole preceding run inside the next piece

parts.note: ult., short for ultimo, means last month; two of them for the plural
in Roman numerals I before C is one less than a hundred

explanation.surface: A painting of the past few months shows people from many different backgrounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Ult. (ultimo) is the old business-letter abbreviation for last month, and Roman 99 is written with the smaller numeral before the larger.
explanation.definitionFit: A multicultural society or group is made up of people drawn from many different ethnic and cultural origins.

clue.text: Atonal opera turning into a strange howling noise

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the opera's name is read backwards

parts.note: Lulu is Alban Berg's atonal opera

indicators.note: something strange is out of its usual form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some atonal opera degenerates into an odd wailing sound, a dig at modern music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Atonal opera' reads as a sneer at modern music in general, but it names one specific work, Berg's Lulu.
explanation.definitionFit: Ululation is a long wavering cry or wail, the sound made by howling animals or mourners.

clue.text: Stay sticky

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to linger or delay
second meaning: an adjective, covered in or like tar

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: one rhymes with 'carry', the other with 'starry'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to linger or delay leaving, while something tarry is smeared with tar and therefore gummy.

clue.text: Overweight tribe making a noise

parts.note: a clan is a tribe or extended family group
read as 'over weight': g for gram, a unit of weight, with the tribe placed over it in this down entry

explanation.surface: A fat tribe makes a racket, perhaps stomping around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overweight' looks like one word describing the tribe, but it splits into 'over' and 'weight'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud ringing metallic sound, a particular kind of noise.

clue.text: Supple Green embracing alternative ethos

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap one's arms around, so one piece hugs the other

parts.note: lime is a shade of green

indicators.note: an alternative version is a different arrangement of the same thing

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Green politician is flexible enough to embrace an alternative philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithesome is a variant of lithe, meaning flexible and graceful in movement.

clue.text: Standard that's OK in Cajun cooking

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something passes muster as acceptable in Louisiana Cajun cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' suggests a level of quality, to fit 'OK', but here it means a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag or banner, and the Union Jack is the national flag of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Joint not beginning to fester

indicators.note: without its beginning, the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to rankle is to fester, as a grievance does

explanation.surface: A joint, perhaps a sore one, that has not yet started to go septic.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint connecting the foot to the leg.

clue.text: Spoil dogsbody taking in bishop receiving zero tolerance

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: taking something into oneself means holding it inside

parts.note: a gofer runs errands; a dogsbody is a British word for a menial drudge
taken as written

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title
O looks like the digit nought

explanation.surface: Someone ruins a junior employee by bringing in a bishop who demands zero tolerance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not part of 'taking in' here: the dogsbody takes the word IN, and the bishop takes zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin of error is the allowance permitted for mistakes or variation, which is what a tolerance means in engineering.

clue.text: Vlad, maybe, giving Ann nasty viral disorder

indicators.note: something in disorder is jumbled, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Vlad passes on a horrible viral illness to someone called Ann, like a vampire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' seems to describe the disease but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Vlad the Impaler, model for Dracula, ruled Wallachia and is linked to Transylvania, so he is an example of someone from there.

clue.text: "Tanks", as in song

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
qua is Latin for 'in the capacity of', i.e. as

explanation.surface: A quoted word, 'tanks', seemingly the title of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Tanks' look like a song title, but it is just the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria is the plural of aquarium, a glass tank for keeping fish.

clue.text: 23's work's wasted on monarchs

parts.note: someone wasted away is thin
K for king and ER for Elizabeth Regina, two monarchs

explanation.surface: A sculptor's work has been wasted on royalty who don't appreciate it.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is RODIN, whose most famous sculpture is The Thinker; 'work's' is 'work is', the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thinker is Auguste Rodin's famous bronze sculpture of a seated man deep in thought.

clue.text: Boat train

parts.note: surface: a train that runs to meet a ferry at a port; setter's reading: one word that can come before both 'boat' and 'train' to make familiar phrases

explanation.walkthrough: A gravy boat is a jug for sauce and a gravy train is an easy source of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Each clue word forms a well-known compound with the answer placed in front, sauce jug and easy money scheme.

clue.text: Bird receiving directions to an edible pod

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it inside

parts.note: the grebe is a diving water bird
E and N are the compass points east and north
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird is pointed towards something it can eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Green beans are the long, slender pods of the bean plant, eaten whole as a vegetable.

clue.text: Heretic going back for African currency

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: an Arian followed Arius, who denied Christ's full divinity, a classic heresy

explanation.surface: A heretic retreats in exchange for money from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The naira is the national currency unit of Nigeria.

clue.text: Statement of charge after a lock-up

indicators.note: after sends the charge to the end, behind the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A formal account of the charges laid after someone is put in a cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock-up' looks like a police cell, but splits into a lock of hair and an instruction to turn it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An assertion is a confident declaration that something is true, a statement or claim.

clue.text: Shame about being rejected for an oath

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: as in 'what a pity', a shame

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the word runs the other way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: It's a pity a sworn promise was refused.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath can mean a swear word or curse, and profanity is blasphemous or obscene language.

clue.text: "Spiritual" — Mondrian? Perhaps "artlessly artistic"

parts.note: Piet Mondrian was the Dutch abstract painter

indicators.note: artless here means without art, so those three letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written, before letters are removed

explanation.surface: A critic muses on whether Mondrian's spiritual art is naive or truly artistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artlessly' sounds like a critical judgement, but it instructs removing ART from the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pietistic describes devout, often emotionally religious feeling, so it fits a sense of spiritual.

clue.text: King travels wearing diamonds that glow

indicators.note: what you wear surrounds you, so the other letters enclose these

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
R for Rex, Latin for king
rides means travels on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: A king travels decked in sparkling diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: The standard spelling is IRIDESCE with one R; the wordplay here builds the double-R form given in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To iridesce is to shimmer with shifting rainbow colours, a kind of glowing.

clue.text: Headless nun found in well in part of France

indicators.note: found inside another word means placed within it

parts.note: 'I'm fine' means I'm well

indicators.note: without a head, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a nun is addressed as Sister

explanation.surface: A beheaded nun is discovered down a well somewhere in France, a gothic mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like a hole in the ground, but means in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: Finistère is a département at the western tip of Brittany, so it is a region of France.

clue.text: Wine and syrup reportedly unavailable to corps de ballet

parts.note: kir is white wine mixed with blackcurrant syrup

indicators.note: what is reported is heard spoken, so this goes by sound not spelling

parts.note: off the menu means unavailable

explanation.surface: Dancers are refused their drinks of wine and cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wine and syrup' looks like two items but together describe a single drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kirov is the famous St Petersburg ballet company, now known again as the Mariinsky.

clue.text: Change the decor after putting out brush fire

indicators.note: putting something out of order scrambles it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: After extinguishing a scrub blaze, the house needs redecorating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting out' reads naturally as extinguishing a fire, but signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To refurbish is to renovate or redecorate a room or building, changing its decor.

clue.text: Instinctive talent for raising Arabic and French money

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: the rial is the money of several Arab states, which 'money' supplies
F is the abbreviation for French
the noun both adjectives qualify; it gives no letters of its own

explanation.surface: A natural gift for raising funds in Arab and French currencies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money' does duty for both: Arabic money is the rial, and the reversal takes in both pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural aptitude or knack for doing something well.

clue.text: Deer with one tongue

parts.note: a hind is a female deer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A deer that has only one tongue, as all deer do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' looks like part of the deer, but means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is a major language of India, and tongue is an old word for a language.

clue.text: Sculptor offering resistance to God

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology

explanation.surface: An artist defies the deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker and The Kiss.

clue.text: Assessed drunk — only semi-teetotal?

indicators.note: teetotal is abbreviated as a doubled letter, and only half of that pair survives here

parts.note: ratted is British slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: Someone judged to be drunk protests they are at least half teetotal.
explanation.walkthrough: Teetotal is TT in crosswords; 'semi' leaves one T of the pair in the slang word, so one of its two Ts is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Rated means assessed or evaluated, given a score or ranking.

clue.text: Some reversible faults in an organ-grinder?

indicators.note: something reversible can be turned the other way, so read the letters backwards
some means a portion, so the letters lie within the clue's words

parts.note: the end of faults, then in an, then the first letter of organ

explanation.surface: A street musician's hand-cranked organ has some faults that can be undone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a smutty joke: the organ being 'ground' is not a barrel organ.
explanation.definitionFit: An onanist is one who masturbates, jocularly pictured as grinding one's own organ.

clue.text: A male feature in North American woman

indicators.note: one piece put in another sits inside it

parts.note: NA is the abbreviation for North American
taken as written
tash is British slang for a moustache

explanation.surface: An American woman sports a distinctly masculine feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Natasha is a Russian girl's name, so it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Big Issue for the third generation?

parts.note: grand means large or big
a person's issue is their offspring

explanation.surface: Copies of The Big Issue, the British magazine sold by homeless vendors, for an older generation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Big Issue is a British street magazine, but 'issue' here means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandchildren are the offspring of one's own sons and daughters, two generations down, counting oneself as first.
